title: Decentralization, central media and corporate power
summary: Concentrated media can manipulate; comparisons to Hitler and record companies.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: I think any country. I went to Germany and the same thing was there. I'm thinking of how that can be thwarted. I think--supposing a strong person did exist who left to laisse faire devices, would accomplish what we just suggested could be accomplished and could be thwarted by the fact of centralized communications network. Maybe he centralizes the wrong thing, because there's been too much said recently about decentralization, so that I have come to suspect very much.

Whenever I hear things like decentralization, I think of people like Ronald Reagan. What alarms me is if you go back to that sort of thing, people seem to forget that we moved away from it just because--
Divide and conquer, among other things.

Yeah, well, you know, decentralization people seem to forget, encompass things like states rights and that was the day when we had segregated everything and people were left alone in many cases to starve.
These very people are not as sympathy oriented as they would like to think; I think there are very selfish motives behind all that.

When you have--in the sense of being centralized communications means that they have that central power and it's the business unit that has the power to buy politicians, for one thing, or if they don't buy them, they have the politicians join them by offering them parts of the company, or in their hugeness, get people to think the way they want them to, because they have the means to cause people to do that. This is what Hitler did.
This is what a big record company--
Of course; that's what I'm trying to say.
Not only record companies, book companies do the same thing, and books are one of the last breed because they're still not that homogenized, although they're fast becoming so.
Something that can really benefit us can turn around and create so much of a problem. It's much more difficult to handle.
We plunge into these things, I guess, in most cases, just without knowing or realizing the perils of it, and if you don't realize that until you're in the thick of it, it's harder.
The so-called freedom that went doesn't wear with this. Increasingly it doesn't. They're destroying themselves, they're destroying the ideaology they most want to preserve.

I'm not going to complain about that. If it sets itself straight, that's all right with me. I'm just concerned that along the way everything gets destroyed and it never gets a chance to straighten out.
That doesn't have a hell of a lot to do with music; does it?
Yes it does. It has everything to do with it.
